Model selection and cross-validation

Source: vignettes/articles/selection.Rmd
selection.Rmd

The example below has 1,000 observations, 5,000 predictors and 100 nonzero coefficients of either sign. It shows a rich coefficient path while retaining a genuinely sparse underlying model.

library(L0glm)
sim <- simul("normal", n=1000L, p=5000L, n_nonzero=100L, seed=42L,
  options=list(beta_range=c(-2, 2)))
X <- sim$X
y <- sim$y

A preset or a tuned path

For a single response the sparse-selection target is

-2\ell(\beta) + \lambda\,\|\beta\|_0.

A preset is often a very effective starting point. Searching a path lets the data choose among the candidate sparse models.

fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, family=gaussian(), lambda="gic")
Preset Penalty per selected coefficient
"aic" 2
"bic" \log n
"gic" \log p\,\log\log n
"ebic" \log n + 2\gamma_{\rm EBIC}\log p
"mbic" \log(np^2/16)

Here p counts selectable predictors, excluding intercepts and mandatory terms. The information-criterion reference gives the parameter-count conventions and literature, including Fan & Tang’s GIC.

gic <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), tune="gic", nlambda=10L,
  prop_range=.25, coefs.true=sim$beta_true, plot=TRUE)
c(lambda_best=gic$lambda_best, lambda_preset=gic$lambda_preset)

The grid focuses on the preset. Use prop_range=1 to explore the full numerical range. The preset often already gives an excellent model, so detailed path tuning can be reserved for cases where it offers a useful improvement.

Method GIC TP FP FN TN F1 MCC
GIC preset 5744 65 0 35 4900 0.788 0.803
Tuned GIC 5536 70 0 30 4900 0.824 0.834
CV minimum 5539 71 0 29 4900 0.830 0.840
CV one-SE 5744 65 0 35 4900 0.788 0.803

Five-fold cross-validation

CV selects the penalty with the lowest mean held-out deviance. Whole rows are held out, including all response channels. Preprocessing, screening and estimated distribution parameters use the training observations in each fold. The default screen="auto" enables ISIS exactly when p_eligible > 10*n, using the training row count n in that fold. The eligible count excludes mandatory terms and predictors excluded by zero starts in every response channel. There is no separate minimum sample size or predictor count.

set.seed(10)
folds <- sample(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(X)))
cv <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), tune="cv", nfolds=5L,
  nlambda=10L, prop_range=.25, foldid=folds, coefs.true=sim$beta_true, plot=TRUE)

The curves use a reversed log10(lambda) axis: strong regularization is on the left, and support sizes appear above the panels. CV error bars show one standard error.

c(lambda_best=cv$lambda_best, lambda_1se=cv$lambda_1se,
  lambda_preset=cv$lambda_preset)
predict(cv$fit_1se, X[1:5, , drop=FALSE], type="response")

fit_best and fit_1se are full-data fits. The one-SE rule chooses the largest lambda with mean deviance within one SE of the minimum. The GIC preset remains available through lambda_preset for comparison.

Validation-based stopping

An independent validation set can choose a predictive checkpoint during a single fit. The training data determine the coefficients, screening and noise parameters. Validation deviance is monitored after each iteration; the fit restores its best checkpoint after a short patience period without improvement. This is available for ordinary GLMs, negative binomial, multinomial and Cox models, and for native nonnegative identity-link Poisson fits.

set.seed(11)
training <- sample.int(nrow(X), floor(.8*nrow(X)))
fit <- l0glmFit(X[training, ], y[training], family=gaussian(),
  lambda="gic", maxit=100L, local.search=FALSE,
  validation=list(X=X[-training, ], y=y[-training]))
fit$validation$selection[c("best_iteration", "iterations", "deviance")]

maxit is a single iteration limit. l0glmTune() searches lambda at that limit; validation stopping lets the predictive fit choose how far to proceed. Keep a separate test set for an independent assessment of predictive accuracy.

Optional local support refinement

Set local.search=TRUE to test additions, deletions and small predictor exchanges after fitting. Screening, compulsory-term updates and original-channel preclustering refits finish first. Every accepted move lowers the fitted penalty’s parameter-count criterion; a supplied independent validation set instead selects by held-out deviance. The original starting exclusions and coefficient constraints remain in force.

fit <- l0glmFit(X, y, lambda="gic", local.search="auto")
fit$local.search[c("applied", "initial.size", "stopping")]
fit$local.search$history
gic <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), tune="gic", nlambda=10L,
  local.search="auto", prop_range=.25)

"auto" limits refinement to models with at most 50 coefficient dimensions after the initial fit. For grouped multichannel fits, each selected row counts its channel dimensions; multinomial rows have one fewer dimension because of their zero-sum constraint. The limit is set with control.local$size.max. "auto" is the default; FALSE disables refinement. See the controls and benchmark examples.

IC paths rank ordinary and special-family models using the same counts as GIC(), AIC() and the other criterion methods. CV independently refines each training fit before evaluating its held-out fold; validation fold responses do not enter the support search.

Random, contiguous and Venetian-blind folds

Without foldid, folds are randomly assigned. Supply a vector to choose a design:

# Five contiguous blocks
folds <- rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(X))[order(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(X)))]

# Venetian blind: odd and even observations alternate
folds <- rep(1:2, length.out=nrow(X))
cv <- l0glmTune(X, y, family=gaussian(), tune="cv",
  foldid=folds, nlambda=10)

For time-dependent observations, choose folds that reflect how predictions will be used. Reserve an independent test set when measuring final predictive accuracy.

Compare methods

sparseGLM() supplies one comparison interface for L0glm, ABESS, L0Learn, LASSO, relaxed LASSO, adaptive variants, MCP and SCAD where supported. The optional biglasso adapter also fits plain LASSO directly on double bigmemory designs; see the file-backed example.

comparison <- sparseGLM(X, y, family=gaussian(),
  method=c("L0glm", "abess", "lasso", "relaxed_lasso"),
  tune="cv", nfolds=5, foldid=sample(rep(1:5, length.out=nrow(X))), nlambda=10)
l0glmMetrics(comparison)

method="all" expands to supported methods for the requested model. The benchmark article reports complete fitting and tuning times.
